ambiguities.readings: The bank's own future deployment is a party statement; a media report of a firm commitment might instead be read as a fact that the decision was made.
Paper counts are optional ecosystem evidence; they may also be treated as a non-business detail because no effect on demand is stated.
The confirmed reactor milestone may be core as a key input-supply milestone; it may be supporting because its effect on NVIDIA's scale is not established.
The agreement to explore is a completed joint decision; the underlying project remains exploratory, which points to supporting weight and possibly a future-facing party statement.
A named publication's report may be a third-party finding of a production milestone; if it is merely reporting a public company announcement, the completed production status is a fact.
The subject is a regulatory decision, suggesting kind 4; the actual speaker is an unnamed source reporting a policy claim, suggesting kind 3.
A research firm's claim about NVIDIA is kind 3 and a third-party view; if the report conveys a confirmed company decision, readers could instead classify the underlying action as kind 1 and fact.
The main company financing aim makes the combined item a party statement; the large amount is anonymous and could make the financing claim a rumour if treated as the main point.
The analysts give a specific consequence of technical setbacks; alternatively, the conditional claim is too general and lacks a reason explaining why the setbacks cap capacity.
A named report's claim of a scrapped configuration is a third-party view; the article's framing as a rumoured setback could make it rumour.
A quantified estimate of a data-center input market is relevant supply evidence; the fragment may be a separate page item with no demonstrated link to NVIDIA's business.
A government investigation into restricted NVIDIA chips is policy evidence; it may fall under the optional Singapore-case treatment if it is part of that case.
The specific explanation of how isolated systems reduce adoption barriers may be a reasoned claim; it may instead be general promotional framing without a concrete result.
The licensing-friction argument offers a specific reason about demand; it may be only the author's unsupported framing of an already announced pricing change.
Downloads are expressly optional ecosystem numbers; the number belongs to a partner platform and may be unrelated to NVIDIA unless a joint-project connection is established.
A report describing NVIDIA's intended arrangement can be read as a third-party view; it can be read as a company plan relayed by the reporter and therefore a party statement.
The headline contains a concrete offer and can be classified as evidence; if the body states the same offer, the headline is not a separate record.
The speaker's forecast about the benefit of an offering is kind 3; if she speaks for NVIDIA about its own offering, the company-self rule points to kind 1.
The sentence is one combined partner development; different named companies are taking distinct actions and may require separate records.
A possible refresh is product-cycle information; an unchanged lineup and speculative refresh without business scale are product details.
The sentence gives a reason that the financing model could unlock customer demand; it can also be read as general background without a concrete claim about its actual effect.

A quantified planned customer deployment is direct demand evidence and may be core; the developer's own project is a future plan without an attributed speaker and may be supporting or a party statement if attributed to the developer.
The earlier quarterly result is optional repetition, while the half-of-sales concentration is a distinct material claim; alternatively, the whole sentence is one combined item and needs one weight.
The financial numbers may be optional restatements of published results; the sentence does not give their period or establish that this article is a later repetition.
Named customers building proprietary silicon are concrete customer actions; the standard's example excludes the general claim that cloud companies' own chips create competition.
A named customer's prior use of NVIDIA chips is customer evidence; without a quantity or new action it may be old background.
The covered company reports another party's future action, suggesting kind 3; the substance is a supplier's own price action, suggesting kind 2.
A regulatory approval is kind 4; a competitor's product milestone is kind 2, and whether it is core depends on its actual importance to the covered drug maker.
A workplace award can be optional under the ecosystem-award example; it can be excluded as descriptive recognition without a business link.
Reported industry shipment data can be a published fact and core demand evidence; if the industry data are an organization's estimate, the source layer is a third-party view.
The refusal itself is excluded; the same sentence also conveys an underlying possible sale that may be retained separately if the report has a source.
A $300 million impairment can be core because it affects profit; it may be supporting if it is small relative to this steelmaker, whose scale is not supplied.
The detail may be optional as part of the Singapore case; it may be excluded as an individual biography unrelated to NVIDIA's drivers.
The Singapore case is optional; new enforcement actions against chip diversion could instead be treated as material policy evidence.
The absence of an accusation against NVIDIA is relevant risk evidence; it is also part of the optional Singapore-case overview.
The financing revenue terms can be classified on their own as core; they may be one record with the plan announcement in U05 rather than a separate item.
The author offers a conditional mechanism and a 12–18 month funding reference; the sentence may be generic explanation without evidence that this plan changes actual timelines.
The sentence makes a specific claim about the financing model and efficiency; it may be promotional or analytical framing without measurable support.
A named tester's numerical comparison with NVIDIA falls within the comparison exception; the exception explicitly mentions a competitor making the comparison, while this tester is independent.
A stock-performance observation is optional market information; the vague assessment may instead be an unsupported author conclusion.

Valar is identified elsewhere in the supplied cases as NVIDIA's study partner, so its reactor milestone may matter to the joint project; the sentence alone does not establish that this reactor is part of that project.

The dated senior appointment can be a concrete company decision and evidence; the evidence standard does not explicitly say whether executive appointments have sufficient business relevance, although §4.3 says they do not open questions.
NVIDIA's rebuttal is a party statement about its own product; the completed act of issuing a rebuttal could be treated as a fact.
IREN investor interest is unrelated to NVIDIA on the supplied sentence; if IREN is a material NVIDIA customer, its financing interest could indirectly affect demand.
A customer's AI growth can be indirect demand evidence; this sentence does not establish that IREN is an NVIDIA customer or quantify purchases.
A forecast of rival chip output is a competitive supply estimate with a date and scale; it may be supporting because it is another company's projected operating quantity rather than NVIDIA demand.
An expert's explicit warning against an apples-to-apples comparison is a competitive claim; it lacks the reason or numerical result required for a specific new judgment.
NVIDIA's warning about Huawei is a concrete claim made in an export-policy discussion; it may be an unsupported and undated general strategic assertion.

A senior commercial appointment is a company decision that may inform demand execution; it may be too routine to affect a business driver, and the standard excludes appointments from opening questions without deciding evidence retention.
Launching a promotional program is a company decision; the free card giveaway may be routine and too small to touch a material driver.
A quantified rate-base forecast can be core if it carries utility earnings; it is supporting if the distant 2028 component lies beyond the relevant question period.

The grocery chain's reported store inflation is its own published figure and thus kind 1 and fact; it can be read as the company's estimate of a market price trend, making it kind 3 and a party statement.
A company-reported sales mix is core quantified revenue evidence; it may be optional if the article is merely restating an already published annual figure, which the case does not establish.
A CEO's qualitative demand assessment is a company statement supporting a key judgment; 'very strong' may be only descriptive language without a number, date or reasoned specific claim.
The subject is an alleged regulatory step, suggesting kind 4; the information is an anonymous claim about what a regulator may do, suggesting kind 3.
The actuary's report of an already occurred loss outcome may be fact; the comparative assessment may be a party statement, and core weight depends on the losses' scale for the insurer.
The falling copper-price rationale makes this a reasoned third-party assessment; the sell recommendation may still be too thin a conclusion without a quantified or dated price change.
Fifteen named large-company customers quantify adoption and could be core demand evidence; absent revenue or contract values, it may only support the demand judgment.
The presentation of trial data is a fact, while the company's interpretation of its own drug data may be a party statement; core weight depends on the drug's importance to the company.

Fuel is expressly an airline cost that can qualify as an A question; cost per seat mile is a ratio rather than the total fuel-cost quantity named in the example, and the case does not establish whether this ratio is the actual dispute.
A House vote on a bill is a checkable policy stage; the case gives no stated connection between Chinese lidar and NVIDIA, so the worth-pursuing test may fail.

FY2028 is within the next-fiscal-year window and the total-revenue question can be rewritten as data-center revenue; the case itself does not state the segment's share or whether other segments can diverge.

If data-center revenue accounts for nearly all business, total revenue folds into the open segment question; if other segments can materially diverge, total revenue may be a distinct question, but the case does not give the needed segment information.

A regulated utility's rate base can be a value-carrying annual main driver and open as A; the A list does not explicitly include rate base, and the catch-all exclusion names events rather than other unlisted quantities.

A regulator's decision on a bank-specific fine is a company-specific regulatory stage under E; a fine may be treated as a litigation or enforcement outcome outside the five classes unless the standard states otherwise.
Whether a tariff remains in force is a policy-stage status that can be checked on a date; it may be a restatement of an already decided extension rather than a new pending regulatory step.

A largest customer's revenue can move independently and materially affect the payments company; the case does not show its scale or why it deserves a separate question instead of evidence for total revenue.

China exposure can be independently important and move separately from total sales; a geographic share may be another cut of the same total and the case does not establish its independent significance.
An annual average copper price is a shared quantity; the standard's settlement examples do not identify which public price series or averaging method settles this question.
